subject: other-disciplines
audience: FE Other Disciplines candidates and engineering students
title: The Relief Valve That Saw 480 N, Not 560
featured_title: THE RELIEF VALVE THAT SAW 480 NEWTONS NOT 560

presentation.challenge: The vessel pressure was 700 kPa absolute, but the valve disk also had atmospheric pressure acting on the opposite side. Net pressure force depended on the 600 kPa differential.

practice.primary_question: How is net pressure force on a relief-valve disk calculated when pressures are given as absolute values on both sides?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Multiplying internal absolute pressure by disk area without subtracting the pressure acting on the opposite side.

case_dna.target_misconception: A relief-valve disk exposed to 700 kPa absolute inside a vessel experiences 700 kPa times area as its net opening pressure force.
case_dna.why_plausible: The internal pressure is the most visible value, but net force depends on pressure acting on both sides of the disk.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: With 700 kPa absolute inside, 100 kPa absolute outside, and area 8 cm², ΔP=600 kPa and F=600000×0.0008=480 N, not 560 N.
case_dna.corrected_model: For opposing uniform pressures, net pressure force is F=(Pin-Pout)A using consistent units.

problem_statement: A pressure-relief valve disk has an effective area of 8.0 cm². The vessel side is at 700 kPa absolute and the discharge side is at 100 kPa absolute. A note calculates 700 kPa×8.0 cm² and reports 560 N as the net opening pressure force. Determine the correct net force due to pressure difference.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Absolute pressure was mistaken for pressure difference.
gates.prompt: What pressure actually drives the net force?

options.label: Use F=(Pin-Pout)A
options.reason: Opposing pressures act on opposite sides of the disk.

options.label: Use F=PinA
options.reason: That ignores the pressure acting on the discharge side.

options.label: Use F=(Pin+Pout)A
options.reason: The opposing pressure forces act in opposite directions.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Resolve forces on both sides of the disk
gates.result: The net pressure force is 480 N.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the net force
gates.success: ΔP=600 kPa and A=0.0008 m², so F=480 N.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Net force depends on pressure difference

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the valve-force note
report: C1. Vessel pressure is 700 kPa absolute.
C3. Therefore net opening pressure force is 560 N.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated internal absolute pressure.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated effective area.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It omits the opposing 100 kPa pressure on the discharge side.

evidence_choices.label: (700-100) kPa×8 cm²=480 N
evidence_choices.reason: The pressure difference determines the net force.

correction.template: The net opening pressure force is {force} N.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Limit net pressure force to 300 N at the same area

options.label: Keep pressure difference at or below 375 kPa
Keep pressure difference at 300 kPa
options.reason: That would produce 240 N, below the stated 300 N limit but is not the maximum allowable differential.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply differential pressure to another disk
gates.prompt: Pin=900 kPa abs, Pout=100 kPa abs, and A=5 cm². What is the net pressure force?

options.label: 400 N
options.reason: ΔP=800 kPa and A=0.0005 m², so F=400 N.

options.label: 450 N
options.reason: That uses only the internal pressure.

gates.explanation: Subtract the opposing absolute pressures before multiplying by area.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the relief-valve force calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that net pressure force depends on pressure difference across the disk rather than internal absolute pressure alone.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Internal absolute pressure was treated as the full net pressure difference.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Atmospheric pressure acts on the opposite side of the disk.
